author: Daniel Worbowski
title: Bryce Underwood's 49-Yard Bomb Wasn't Enough, and No. 18 Michigan Fans Are Sick About It - NewsBreak
text:
By Daniel Worbowski ,
9 hours ago Nfl logo on gradient background — Created by the Sports On Tap desk | Source : Sports On Tap (team logos property of their respective owners) No. 17 Iowa pulled off a brutal 20-19 upset against No. 18 Michigan on Saturday, stealing the win in a last-second stunner at Michigan Stadium. This one stings, folks, especially after the Wolverines had battled back to take the lead late in the game.
Underwood Was Dealing, Y’all Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood, sporting number 19, has been on a whole different level since his rough 2026 debut against Western Michigan. Seriously, the guy has looked so much more competent and poised running that offense, and it showed big time against Iowa. He jumped out to a super fast start, connecting on eight of his first ten throws for 118 yards and a touchdown. Honestly, if Salesi Moa hadn’t dropped Underwood’s second pass, that completion percentage would’ve been even higher.
Credit has to go to Coordinator Jason Beck, too. He’s been putting Underwood in positions to succeed, dialing up designed rollouts that give him clear throwing lanes downfield. And Beck got creative, deploying Underwood in a Wildcat package, lining him up out wide and having him flash across the formation in a jet motion. We even saw Underwood take a handoff from running back Jordan Marshall and then complete an 11-yard pass to Andrew Marsh. Later, Beck dipped into his bag of tricks again, calling a flea-flicker that Underwood executed perfectly, feathering a layered pass to JJ Buchanan for a huge 32-yard gain. Underwood was absolutely cooking.
Heartbreak After a Heroic Strike But Underwood’s absolute best was still to come. In the fourth quarter, after Iowa had actually taken a one-point lead, our guy wasn’t rattled. He maneuvered in the pocket like a magician, evaded a few oncoming rushers, and then delivered an incredible 49-yard strike to Buchanan. That play put the Wolverines ahead 19-14. At that point, it felt like his touchdown pass was absolutely going to carry Michigan to its fourth win of the season.
Alas, it was not meant to be. The game ended in a gut-wrenching 20-19 loss for Michigan, a true last-second stunner that the original headline pointed to as a costly special teams flub. It’s just a brutal way to lose when your quarterback played his heart out. Underwood finished the game with 17 completions on 28 attempts, an impressive 276 passing yards, two touchdowns, and one interception. Even with the loss, he absolutely authored one of the best performances of his career.
What a day for Bryce Underwood, even if the result for Coach Kyle Whittingham and the Wolverines was pure heartbreak. That kind of individual effort deserved a win, but sometimes the ball just doesn’t bounce your way.
